headline: On the infrastructure lens the v5.0 proposal is not smarter than us — it is materially less informed, and in one place it is unsafe. Its cost table ("Supabase — free up to 500MB") omits every fact that decides the question: Free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity, Free has NO automated backups, and Free allows only 2 active projects. Its §9.3 schema is created with raw `CREATE TABLE` and never enables RLS, which per Supabase's own docs leaves every user's `events` and `user_fleet` world-readable and world-writable via the anon key that ships in our client — a critical breach by construction. And we already ran this evaluation better on 2026-07-15: `docs/research/04a-architecture.md:37` names Supabase and rejects it verbatim — "Supabase (Pro $25/mo, pauses after 7d idle — landmine)" — choosing Cloudflare D1 on the same $5 Workers bill. The proposal does not engage that finding. My verdict: Supabase = NEVER as specified, LATER only on a named trigger and then probably D1 instead; engine-in-Worker = REJECT as the primary compute path, ADAPT a narrow read-only safety-adjudicator slice after P0-worker ships.
isItSmarter:
WORSE on infrastructure, with one genuine point in its favour.

WORSE — cost. The proposal's §9.5 table is the whole of its infrastructure economics: "Supabase | PostgreSQL + JSONB + Realtime + Auth | חינם עד 500MB". Verified against supabase.com/pricing today: Free is 500MB DB, 5GB egress, 50k MAU, 200 peak Realtime connections, 500k Edge invocations, 1GB Storage — AND "Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity" AND "Limit of 2 active projects". Verified against supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups: the Free plan gets NO automated backups; Supabase tells free users to run `db dump` themselves. So the proposal's headline claim that Supabase gives us "backup" is false on the tier it prices. A seasonal BBQ app on Free will be found paused on the first warm Saturday after a quiet fortnight. Anything you would call production is $25/mo from day one, not $0.

WORSE — it re-litigates a decision we made better. `docs/research/04a-architecture.md` (2026-07-15, "verified against primary docs") reached the opposite conclusion with reasoning the proposal never addresses: §3 "One $5/mo Cloudflare bill covers all three, zero egress… Cloudflare wins unambiguously and matches the existing seam", and line 37 explicitly disposes of the candidate: "Supabase (Pro $25/mo, pauses after 7d idle — landmine)". My independent check of the pricing page confirms that 2-week-old finding is still exactly right.

WORSE — it is internally contradictory. §9.2 says "Cloudflare: PWA Front-End (Offline-First/LocalStorage) + Cloudflare Worker = מנוע החוקים v5.0". You cannot be offline-first while your rules engine is a cross-origin HTTP call. Our own service worker settles it: `dist/sw.js:8` — `if(url.origin!==location.origin) return;  // leave cross-origin (fonts/AI) alone`. A Worker-hosted engine is cross-origin, therefore uncached, therefore dead offline, by the deliberate design of the SW we already shipped. The user is standing in a yard next to a smoker for 12 hours on flaky mobile data. That is the worst possible place to put a network round-trip on the critical path.

WORSE — its SQL-vs-NoSQL case (§9.1) solves a problem we do not have and its example is one we forbid. We have no server DB at all, so "Foreign Keys מונעים פרופיל ציוד עם מכשיר שלא קיים → מונע קריסות Runtime" is arguing for a runtime guard we replaced with a stronger build-time one: `equipment_map.py` derives the `equip` block for all 279 recipes against a 27-token vocabulary matched 1:1 to `EQUIP_CATS`+`EQUIP_OTHER_ITEMS` (27 references in app.js), and Guards A/B/C fail the BUILD. A build failure blocks the release; an FK violation surfaces in production for one user. Worse, its motivating example — "עדכון גלובלי (טמפ' בטיחות עוף 74°C→73°C) = שורה אחת" — is precisely what CLAUDE.md and DoD-10 forbid. `data.py` carries `safe=74` bound to a citation in `sources.py` merged at build time; a one-row UPDATE to a safety temperature is not a convenience, it is the removal of a safety value from the guard regime that protects it.

WORSE — its security model. See the audit in `reject`. Briefly: no RLS anywhere in the document (zero occurrences of RLS / ROW LEVEL / policy in the whole file), a `user_id REFERENCES auth.users(id)` FK mistaken for an authorization control, and an unauthenticated-looking `/iot-telemetry` Edge Function holding SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which by Supabase's own definition bypasses RLS entirely.

SMARTER — one real thing, and I will not defend our side on it. §6 correctly identifies a capability that CANNOT be built client-side at any price: ingesting thermometer telemetry and firing an alert **while the app is closed**. Our system brief has no answer to that; a PWA with a suspended tab cannot poll a vendor cloud. That is a genuine, honest gap and the only argument in the entire document that actually requires a backend. Its chosen mechanism is still wrong (see reject #4), but the requirement it names is real and we should write it down.

NEUTRAL — Workers dollar cost. The proposal's "חינם עד 100K בקשות/יום" for Workers is accurate (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits: 100,000/day Free). Running an engine there is genuinely cheap in money. The expensive things are latency, offline, and a new failure mode — none of which the proposal prices. It also misses the constraint that actually bites: Free gives **10 ms CPU per invocation**. Our `eqmValidity` runs `EQM.ownership` over EVERY `itemPaths` entry, and app.js:1780-1794 documents that we added two caches specifically because this ran ~279 times per catalog paint. A batch endpoint validating the catalog would exceed 10ms comfortably, so "free" is off the table for the very design the proposal implies.

adopt.item: Write down IoT-while-app-is-closed as a named, backend-only capability gap in the gap map — the one thing §6 gets right that we have no answer to.
adopt.why: §6 is correct that a suspended PWA cannot ingest telemetry or alert the user while closed. This is the ONLY requirement in the proposal that genuinely cannot be met client-side, and it is currently absent from our 141-gap map. Naming it converts a vague 'maybe we need a backend someday' into a specific trigger condition we can test against later, which is what turns the Supabase question from a taste debate into a dated decision.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: docs/analysis/2026-07-27-gap-closing-BIG-STATUS.md — a new row in the S6 (infrastructure) band, status OPEN, phase P10, cross-referenced to docs/research/04a-architecture.md §2(b). No code changes.

adopt.item: Ship P0-worker (B19-B22 / E14 / H-3) BEFORE any conversation about giving the Worker more responsibility.
adopt.why: Not from the proposal, but the proposal forces the issue: it wants to put the rules engine on a perimeter that is currently known-broken. worker/index.js:56 `catch { rec = { active: true }; }` turns a corrupted KV record into an UNCAPPED, permanently-active code; :43 admits `streamGenerateContent` which the `JSON.parse(text)` meter at :77-86 silently skips (documented cap bypass, B19); the read at :53 and write at :84 straddle an `await fetch` (TOCTOU, already RED-characterised in worker/test/index.spec.js:172 'D3 — metering is a check-then-act race'); :66 has no AbortController; :21 CORS is `'*'`; :39 health leaks `hasKey`. All are logged OPEN and P0-worker is NOT STARTED. Every one of these is a direct cost or security defect on the boundary that would host the engine.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: worker/index.js (all seven sites above); worker/test/index.spec.js already holds the RED tests, including the `it.fails` at :59 that turns green-as-red when the fail-open is fixed. Also KV: free tier is 1,000 writes/day to distinct keys and 1 write/sec to the SAME key, which makes the per-code counter racy by construction — the fix needs an atomic primitive (Durable Object) or debit-first accounting, not a bigger KV.

adapt.why: The shape is right and it already matches what we have: `mk-events` (app.js:9623 `evList`), `mk-tlstate-*`, `mk-cook-live-*` are all opaque per-event blobs. A live cook is one document that changes as a unit; normalising it into rows buys nothing and costs joins. This is also exactly what our own 04a-architecture.md §4.2 concluded independently — 'blob per user id, LWW on updatedAt' — so the proposal and our prior research agree here.
adapt.whatMustChange: Take the JSONB blob shape, drop the relational half (`user_fleet` as a table, FKs as integrity). Put the blob on Cloudflare D1 behind the Worker we already own, not on Supabase — same $5 bill, zero egress, no 7-day pause. And do NOT put journal photos in it: app.js:4547 stores `e.photo = await downscale(f)` in mk-journal, so a naive 'sync everything' pushes user-generated images into a store we would then be the controller of.

adapt.item: 'Cloudflare Worker = מנוע החוקים v5.0' (§9.2) — the idea of engine logic running server-side.
adapt.why: As stated it is wrong (it kills offline and adds a round-trip to a yard-with-flaky-4G use case). But there is a narrow, real version of it, and it is OUR idea already: docs/research/04a-architecture.md §2(a) says the proxy should 're-apply grounding/validation contract server-side (moves the safety discipline behind a boundary users can't bypass)'. Once we take money, a client-side safety guard is bypassable by the person we are liable to.
adapt.whatMustChange: Invert it. The client keeps the engine as the primary compute path — always, offline, zero latency. The Worker gets a READ-ONLY copy of the safety floors plus `aiSafetyNums` plus the Phase-3a `action_id` contract, and its only job is to REJECT an AI response whose numbers do not match. Validation, never generation. Gate on P0-worker being shipped and on the first paying subscriber existing. Scope is a few hundred lines, not the 400-line UniversalCulinaryEngine of §4.5.

adapt.item: The IoT ingestion mechanism (§6.1 א — 'Edge Function פונה לענן היצרן כל דקה').
adapt.why: The requirement is real (see adopt #1); the mechanism is a credential-custody liability. MEATER's public cloud REST API is documented as BETA and authenticates with a JWT obtained from a login endpoint — not OAuth. So 'poll the manufacturer's cloud' means our server must hold the user's MEATER account email and password, or a long-lived token derived from them, for every user. Its own guidance is 2 requests/60s recommended (60 max), per account, so a fleet poller is N authenticated sessions. Taking custody of another vendor's account passwords to power a convenience feature is a liability we do not have today.
adapt.whatMustChange: Never store third-party account credentials. Accept only (a) vendor-initiated webhooks into an authenticated endpoint of ours, where the vendor supports them, or (b) the proposal's own option ב/ג — user-initiated CSV/JSON upload via the File System Access API, and the manual-override button — both of which are 100% client-side, need no backend, and can be built today. Revisit (a) only if a specific vendor ships OAuth or webhooks.

reject.defect: CRITICAL. It creates `user_fleet` and `events` in the public schema via raw `CREATE TABLE` and never enables Row Level Security. Supabase's own documentation is unambiguous: 'RLS is enabled by default on tables created with the Table Editor in the dashboard. If you create one in raw SQL or with the SQL editor, remember to enable RLS yourself.' Without RLS, PostgREST exposes both tables to the `anon`/publishable role — the key that by definition ships inside our client PWA. Any user, or anyone who opens devtools, can SELECT and UPDATE every other user's events: event names, `target_serve_time`, `guest_count`, and the entire `live_timeline`. Separately, `user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id)` is being used as if it were an access control. It is not. A foreign key guarantees the row points at *a* user; nothing stops user B inserting a row carrying user A's UUID. That requires an RLS policy with `USING (auth.uid() = user_id)` and `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id)`, neither of which appears anywhere.
reject.evidence: grep over the entire PROPOSAL file for `RLS|ROW LEVEL|SERVICE_ROLE|policy` returns ZERO hits outside the word 'Supabase' itself. Supabase docs (guides/database/postgres/row-level-security, guides/api/api-keys), fetched 2026-07-29: 'Once you have enabled RLS, no data will be accessible via the API when using a publishable key, until you create policies.'

reject.defect: CRITICAL. The service_role key bypasses RLS entirely — Supabase: service keys 'can be used to bypass RLS' and 'should never be used in the browser or exposed to customers'. Server-side is the right place for it, so that part is fine. The defect is that once you hold it, the Edge Function becomes the ONLY authorization boundary, and the proposal describes no authentication on the endpoint at all: 'POST /iot-telemetry → שליפת live_timeline מ-Supabase → עדכון הנתח → הרצת חוקי זמן-אמת → שמירת JSONB → trigger_push_notification'. An unauthenticated endpoint holding a service-role client is a full read/write oracle over every user's data: POST an arbitrary `event_id` with an arbitrary temperature and you rewrite a stranger's cook plan and fire a push notification at them. Combined with defect #1 (no RLS), there is no second line of defence anywhere in the design.
reject.evidence: PROPOSAL §6.3, lines 513-518. No auth check, no JWT verification, no per-user scoping appears in the described flow. Supabase docs guides/api/api-keys, fetched 2026-07-29.

reject.defect: Materially misleading. It prices a tier that cannot host this product. Verified on supabase.com/pricing 2026-07-29: Free = 'Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity' and 'Limit of 2 active projects'. Verified on supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups: Free gets NO automated backups — Supabase instructs free users to export via `db dump` themselves. So the proposal's own claimed benefit (backup) does not exist at the price it quotes; a seasonally-used BBQ app will be found paused; and 2 projects means prod + dev with nothing left for CI, which would push the 816-test suite at the production database. Realistic floor for anything production-shaped is Pro at $25/mo — 5x the entire Cloudflare bill our own research already costed.
reject.evidence: supabase.com/pricing and supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups, both fetched 2026-07-29. Compare docs/research/04a-architecture.md:37, written 2026-07-15 from primary docs: 'Supabase (Pro $25/mo, pauses after 7d idle — landmine)'.

reject.item: §9.2 — 'Cloudflare Worker = מנוע החוקים v5.0' as the primary compute path.
reject.defect: It breaks offline, and our own service worker proves it. dist/sw.js line 8: `if(url.origin!==location.origin) return;   // leave cross-origin (fonts/AI) alone`. A Worker-hosted engine is cross-origin, so it is never cached and never available without network — while the same §9.2 line simultaneously labels the PWA 'Offline-First/LocalStorage'. The two halves of one sentence contradict each other. It also inverts a performance decision we already made and documented: app.js:1780-1794 explains that `eqmResolveCached` and `eqmDefaultReqOwn` exist because `eqmRequiresChip` + `eqInvState` each ran resolveItem over ~279 cards per catalog paint. Every one of those synchronous in-process calls becomes a network call, plus a loading state, plus an error state that does not exist today — and each new error string must pass Guard A in 7 (soon 23) languages. Cloudflare Free also caps CPU at 10ms per invocation, which a batched catalog validation would exceed.
reject.evidence: dist/sw.js:8; app.js:1780-1794 (the caching rationale); PROPOSAL §9.2 line 569; developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits (Free: 10 ms CPU/invocation).

reject.item: §9.1 — 'עדכון גלובלי (טמפ' בטיחות עוף 74°C→73°C) = שורה אחת' as an argument FOR SQL.
reject.defect: This is the proposal's most dangerous sentence for us, and it is dangerous precisely because it sounds like a feature. Our chicken/turkey safety value is `safe=74` in data.py, bound to a primary-source citation in sources.py (279 citations) and merged at build time. CLAUDE.md makes it non-negotiable that every `safe` value traces to a cited source; DoD-10 makes altering one a gated event requiring a named assertion. Moving safety values into a runtime-mutable table removes them from the build-time guard regime — no Guard B unit check, no test, no citation link, no review. A one-row UPDATE that silently lowers a pasteurization temperature is exactly the failure mode our entire discipline exists to prevent.
reject.evidence: data.py line 3 header ('keys: n,cat,heb,eng,kg,svt,svh,smt,smh,tgt,safe,…') and the shawarma row `tgt=75,safe=74`; sources.py CUT_SOURCES merged at build; CLAUDE.md 'Safety values trace to primary sources'; PROPOSAL §9.1 line 561.

reject.item: The claim that the 816-test suite is unaffected (implicit throughout §9).
reject.defect: It is not addressed at all, and it is the largest hidden cost. Every test today runs against a self-contained static document: tests/_fixtures.ts:95-100 serves dist/index.html from memory via `route.fulfill`, and playwright.config.ts:54 deliberately severs external network (`--host-resolver-rules=MAP fonts.googleapis.com 127.0.0.1, MAP fonts.gstatic.com 127.0.0.1`) with `retries: 0` and a 30s test ceiling. Introducing a server dependency forces one of two things: a new Supabase/engine mocking fixture layer threaded through many of the 126 spec files, or real network calls inside a zero-retry 30s budget. The second option is disqualified by CLAUDE.md §11a and DoD-11/12 and would recreate the exact flake class the project already spent a full arc eliminating (docs/research/flake-refactor-rootcause.md, suite 3.0m → ~54s).
reject.evidence: tests/_fixtures.ts:88-101; playwright.config.ts:15,24,36,54; 126 spec files under tests/.

impactOnUs:
If adopted as written, concretely:

BREAKS — offline. `dist/sw.js:8` never caches cross-origin, so a Worker-hosted engine means `itemStages`/`itemPaths`/`effectiveSchedule` (app.js:4094, 4176, 4194) and `eqmValidity`/`EQM.ownership`/`EQM.availability` (equipment.js:330-435) stop working with no network. The catalog's per-card `eqmRequiresChip` (app.js:1816) and `eqInvState` render paths would each need a new loading and error state, i.e. new user-facing strings through `L()` — every one of which must pass Guard A in 7 active languages (1535 keys × 6 today) and Guard B's numeric/unit safety check.

BREAKS — the citation pipeline and DoD-10. `sources.py`'s 279 citations are merged into the data at BUILD time and inlined into `dist/index.html` (7.79MB raw / 2.18MB gzipped). Moving recipe/safety data into Postgres moves `safe=` values out of the artifact the build guards can inspect, which makes DoD-10 ("no `bcheck` stage, `temp`, `safe` value, or cook duration altered") unverifiable statically. `bcheck` is generated from `meta.obj.safe` at app.js:4167 — that line reads inlined build-time data today.

BREAKS — the test architecture. tests/_fixtures.ts:95-100 (`route.fulfill` from `dist/index.html`) and playwright.config.ts:54 (network severed) assume a self-contained document. 126 spec files, 816 tests, `retries: 0`.

NEW LIABILITY — personal data. app.js:4547 stores downscaled user PHOTOS in `mk-journal`; `mk-events` (app.js:9623), `mk-inventory` (app.js:10068), `mk-journal` (app.js:4531) plus ~60 `mk-*` keys are all local today. Syncing them makes us a data controller under GDPR and Israeli PPL Amendment 13 — a fact our own research already flagged (docs/research/04a-architecture.md:42) and the proposal never mentions. That means a DPA with Supabase, a deletion path, a privacy notice, and consent copy — in 7 languages heading to 23.

DISPLACES — the roadmap. Per OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF §9 the queue is CP2 → E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 → orchestrator (P8), against ~100 still-open gaps. A Supabase adoption consumes that entire lane.

WHAT I WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE INSTEAD, now: (1) ship P0-worker against worker/index.js:21,39,43,53,56,66,84 with the RED tests already sitting in worker/test/index.spec.js; (2) build the encrypted export/import from docs/research/04a-architecture.md §4.1 — a single JSON download/upload, zero infrastructure, which kills the "I lost my journal" fear that is the only user-visible pain a database would solve today; (3) add the IoT-while-closed gap row to docs/analysis/2026-07-27-gap-closing-BIG-STATUS.md. Nothing else.

risks.risk: Adopting §9.3 as written ships a public read/write breach of every user's event data from day one. No RLS + the anon key in the client = `SELECT * FROM events` for anyone who opens devtools.
risks.mitigation: Do not adopt the schema. If Supabase is ever adopted, the non-negotiable order is: enable RLS on every public-schema table FIRST, write `USING (auth.uid() = user_id)` and `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id)` policies, run Supabase's Security Advisor, and add a CI check that fails if any public table has `relrowsecurity = false`. Treat 'a table exists without RLS' as a build-breaking defect exactly as Guard A treats an untranslated key.

risks.risk: The §6.3 Edge Function holds SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with no authentication shown. That key bypasses RLS entirely, so a single missing auth check on `/iot-telemetry` is a total compromise of all user data, and a leaked key is unrecoverable without rotating and redeploying everything.
risks.mitigation: Never write an endpoint that combines a service-role client with an unauthenticated route. Verify the caller's JWT and scope every query by `auth.uid()` even when using the service role. Better: do not take the service role at all — use the user's own JWT so RLS remains the enforcement layer and the Edge Function cannot be the single point of failure.

risks.risk: Free-tier project pausing after 1 week of inactivity. A seasonal BBQ product will routinely go quiet for a fortnight; the first user of the season opens the app mid-cook and the backend is asleep.
risks.mitigation: Never run anything user-facing on Supabase Free. Budget $25/mo from the first real user, or use Cloudflare D1 which has no such concept. If Supabase Free is used for prototyping only, say so explicitly and never let a live cook depend on it.

risks.risk: Putting the rules engine behind a network call turns a currently-impossible failure (engine unavailable) into a routine one, in the worst possible context — a 12-hour cook in a yard on flaky mobile data, where the answers are safety-relevant.
risks.mitigation: Keep the engine client-side, permanently. If server-side logic is ever added, it must be strictly additive (validate/reject an AI answer) and the client must degrade to its local result when the Worker is unreachable, never to a blank state.

risks.risk: Adding responsibility to worker/index.js before P0-worker ships. The Worker already fails OPEN on a corrupted KV record (`catch { rec = { active: true }; }` at :56 → uncapped, permanently-active access), lets `streamGenerateContent` bypass metering (:43 vs :77-86), has a TOCTOU on the usage counter (:53/:84 across an await), no upstream timeout (:66), CORS `*` (:21), and leaks `hasKey` (:39). More surface on that perimeter multiplies the blast radius.
risks.mitigation: Hard gate: no new Worker responsibility until B19-B22 / E14 / H-3 are closed with the RED tests in worker/test/index.spec.js turned green. This is worth doing regardless of the v5.0 decision.

risks.risk: Third-party credential custody for IoT (§6.1 א). MEATER's public API is BETA and uses JWT-from-login, not OAuth, so server-side polling requires holding users' MEATER account credentials.
risks.mitigation: Refuse credential storage as a standing policy. Ship §6.1 options ב (file upload) and ג (manual override) instead — both are pure client-side and buildable today. Accept vendor-initiated webhooks only, and only where a vendor offers them.

risks.risk: Making safety values runtime-mutable (§9.1's 'one row update'), removing them from the build-time citation and Guard regime.
risks.mitigation: Absolute rule: safety values (`safe`, `tgt`, `bcheck` targets, cook durations) stay in data.py + sources.py and are baked at build. Any database, if one arrives, holds USER state only — events, fleet, journal — never recipe or safety data. Write this into CLAUDE.md as an explicit boundary before any DB work starts.

risks.risk: Test-suite erosion. A server dependency introduced without a mocking layer will produce intermittent failures, which CLAUDE.md §11a/DoD-12 correctly classify as bugs — leading either to a long debugging arc or, worse, to quiet pressure to re-enable retries.
risks.mitigation: Any backend work must land with its fixture/mock layer in the same phase, and the suite must stay network-free. `retries: 0` is not negotiable.

risks.risk: Vendor lock-in and migration cost. Supabase Auth (`auth.users`), RLS policies, and Realtime are not portable; leaving later means rewriting the authorization model, not just moving rows.
risks.mitigation: Prefer Cloudflare D1 behind our own Worker: the authorization logic lives in code we own and the data is plain SQLite. If Supabase is chosen, keep all authorization expressible in one place and avoid coupling application logic to `auth.users`.

risks.risk: GDPR / Israeli PPL exposure created the moment user photos and event data leave the device.
risks.mitigation: Adopt 04a-architecture.md §4.3 — client-side encrypt the blob with a key derived from a user passphrase, so we hold ciphertext and cannot read it. This also becomes a marketing asset ('end-to-end encrypted journal') consistent with the BYOK positioning. Do this before any sync, not after.

costEstimate:
Realistic cost model. Assumptions stated so you can argue with them: an "active user" does ~2 cooks/month, seasonally concentrated at weekends; engine traffic is batched (one request per catalog paint, not 279).

ENGINE IN THE WORKER — dollars are NOT the problem.
· 100 users (~20k req/mo, <1k/day): $0, Free tier.
· 1,000 users (~200k req/mo, ~7k/day mean): $0, still Free — though weekend bursts eat headroom.
· 10,000 users (~2M req/mo, ~67k/day mean, weekend peaks over the 100k/day Free cap): Workers Paid, $5/mo. Includes 10M requests + 30M CPU-ms; at ~5ms/request we would use ~10M CPU-ms, comfortably inside. Overage beyond that is $0.30/M requests, $0.02/M CPU-ms.
· The hard constraint is not money: Free allows only **10 ms CPU per invocation**. A batched catalog validation exceeds that, so the "free" story collapses into $5/mo immediately — which is still trivial. Read that as: the Worker engine is cheap and still a bad idea, for offline/latency reasons, not cost.

SUPABASE — the proposal says $0; the truth is $25/mo minimum for anything real.
· 100 users: technically inside every Free quota (500MB DB, 5GB egress, 50k MAU, 200 Realtime, 500k Edge, 1GB Storage). But Free pauses after 1 week idle, has NO automated backups, and caps you at 2 active projects (prod + dev = nothing for CI). Honest cost: **$25/mo Pro** on day one. Storage is the first real squeeze — journal photos at ~20 × 200KB/user = ~4MB/user → ~400MB, i.e. ~40% of the 1GB Free allowance from 100 users alone.
· 1,000 users: DB ~0.3-1GB/yr crosses the 500MB Free line inside year one; photo storage ~4GB crosses 1GB Free outright. **$25/mo Pro** (8GB DB, 100GB storage, 250GB egress all included). ~$25-30/mo.
· 10,000 users: DB ~3-10GB (may tip past 8GB → $0.125/GB), egress ~50GB (inside 250GB), MAU 10k (inside 100k), storage ~40GB (inside 100GB). But Realtime peak concurrent is 500 on Pro, and 10k weekend-concentrated cooks will exceed that. **~$25-45/mo**, plus **~$100/mo for 7-day PITR** if losing a day of live-cook data is unacceptable — Pro alone gives only 7 daily backups, no point-in-time. Realistic band **$25-$135/mo**.
· Compare: Cloudflare Pages (free) + one Worker + D1, all on **$5/mo**, zero egress charges ever, no pause, no separate auth vendor. That is the comparison docs/research/04a-architecture.md §3 already made.
· Gemini remains the dominant COGS in every scenario (~$0.02-0.05/cook per that research), which neither architecture changes.

ENGINEERING COST — this is what actually hurts.
· Supabase adoption done properly: schema + RLS policies + a policy-coverage CI check + auth flow + session handling + migrations + client sync layer + LWW conflict resolution + a mocking fixture threaded through the 126 spec files + privacy notice, consent and deletion path in 7 languages (heading to 23, each through Guards A/B/C) + a DPA. **LARGE** — multiple weeks of the project's cycles.
· Engine-in-Worker: **LARGE** and mostly negative value now (loading/error states per card, new i18n surface, offline regression, test rework).
· P0-worker hardening: **MEDIUM**, and worth doing whatever you decide about v5.0.
· Encrypted export/import (04a §4.1): **SMALL-MEDIUM**, zero infrastructure, and it addresses the only user-visible pain ("I lost my journal") that a database would solve today.

WHAT IT DISPLACES: per OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF §9 the queue is CP2 (planned, awaiting your decision) → E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 → orchestrator P8, against ~100 open gaps. A Supabase programme consumes that whole lane and delivers no new cooking capability.

RECOMMENDATION.
· Supabase: **NEVER as specified**; LATER only on a trigger, and even then evaluate D1 first.
· Engine into the Worker: **NEVER as the primary path**; LATER as a read-only AI-output adjudicator only.
